punchline: The more of an expert you become, the harder it can get to ask a basic question about your own field.
thirty_sec: Warren Berger makes an awkward point about expertise. The more you know about a field, the fewer basic questions you ask, because you already know how things work. But that knowledge carries assumptions you stop noticing. Newcomers still see them, which is why their naive questions can be so useful. His fix: look at your own field like a beginner, and check how other fields solve similar problems.
question: What's something in your line of work that everyone just accepts and nobody really questions?
